name: LinkedIn Search Scraper
description: Paste a LinkedIn search URL (people, companies or posts) and export every result LinkedIn shows you: profiles with name, headline, location, photo and connection degree; company pages with industry, location, logo and follower counts; posts with their full text, author, permalink and publication date. You connect your own LinkedIn account and the scraper browses with it, exactly like you would in your browser. LinkedIn caps every search at about 1,000 results (use filters or several searches to slice a bigger query). Optional add-ons open each profile, each company page or each post once to add the full details.

name: LinkedIn Company Employees Scraper
description: Scrape employees of any LinkedIn company from its company URL: full name, headline, profile URL, location, photo, connection degree and the company they were matched on. You connect your own LinkedIn account and the scraper browses with it, exactly like you would in your browser. LinkedIn caps this search at 1,000 employees per company (use the keyword filter to slice bigger companies), and profiles that are too distant from your network come back as 'LinkedIn Member' with no name or profile URL - measured at around 10% of rows on a well-connected account, more on a fresh or weakly-connected one.

name: LinkedIn Jobs Scraper

name: Glassdoor Jobs Scraper
description: Give us a Glassdoor job search URL — or just a keyword and a location — and we will export every job posting with the full description, salary estimate, apply link and the complete company profile with all of its Glassdoor ratings. Reads Glassdoor's public job search, no account required, zero risk.

name: Crunchbase Companies Scraper
description: Give us a Crunchbase company URL or a Crunchbase company search, and we export the company profile: description, website, industries, headquarters, employee range, contacts, founders, investors, funding rounds, acquisitions, products, growth and heat scores, and the technology and intent data Crunchbase publishes. No Crunchbase account and no cookies. Two limits come straight from Crunchbase and apply to everyone who is not on a paid Crunchbase plan. First, a search returns at most 15 companies: Crunchbase serves a single page of 15 and refuses to paginate, so a search task exports 15 companies at most, however many matches it reports. Use the filters (industry, location, founded year, funding stage, employee count, operating status, company type, IPO status) to cut your market into as many 15-company windows as you need, or feed company URLs, which have no such limit. Second, the founding date and valuations are never served to a free session, and funding amounts are only published for a minority of companies: Crunchbase still shows the amount of a recent round on the public activity timeline of about one company in seven, and gates it everywhere else, so the funding amount fields are filled when it does and empty when it does not. One display note: the Results tab of your dashboard only shows the fields of the Company details option when that option is on, and it is off by default because on a search it costs one extra request per company. Company URLs return those fields for free on the very first request, and nothing is ever lost: the stored row, the CSV and the API export always carry every field we collected, whatever the toggle says.
